title: Kelly, Kornienko Land on Earth after Year in Space
main_content:
Scott Kelly and Mikhail Kornienko have their feet on the ground for the first time in 340 days.

Riding in a Russian spacecraft, they made it back to Kazakhstan.

Theirs was a record-setting journey. It is the longest time humans have spent living on the International Space Station (ISS).

After being taken out of the capsule, they were put in special chairs while they start getting used to Earth’s gravity again.

After undergoing more tests and exams at NASA’s Houston, Texas offices, Kelly said he wants to go home and jump into his swimming pool.

In his last press conference from space, Kelly talked about the difficulties of living on the ISS for a year. He called it “a harsh environment,” with only a small personal space.

He said he feels “pretty good physically.” But the toughest part was being away from loved ones.

Kelly and Kornienko performed scientific experiments including growing flowers and lettuce. The space station tested how humans endure long-term space flights.
